method: Every candidate issue was re-read in full (title, body, first comments) via `gh issue view`; raw text archived in research/v3/rq2_issue_texts.json (accessed 2026-11-20). Each item is labelled by what the thread itself shows, not by search-query category. AI-assisted reading; the author must confirm each label before submission.

included.evidence: Reporter observed PG::UndefinedColumn on old processes still running after a column-rename finalisation, before new code was deployed; root cause traced to explicit column enumeration triggered by pre-existing ignored_columns.

included.class: Observed missing-column crash (root cause not confirmed in thread)
included.evidence: Self-hosted 25.7.0 on Kubernetes: snuba consumer fails with UndefinedColumn for sentry_monitor.is_upserting. Thread does not establish whether the cause was version skew between components or an incomplete migration.

included.class: Single-file linter false positive on a two-release Contract
included.evidence: Valid SeparateDatabaseAndState two-migration removal flagged; maintainer acknowledges SeparateDatabaseAndState is not handled and notes the pair is only safe if deployed separately (a cross-release property).

Maintainer lists as 'decided against': not requiring safety_assured for remove_column when ignored_columns is detected, because ignored_columns is typically removed after the drop runs, which a single-file check cannot reason about.
User asks why ignored_columns + safety_assured remove_column cannot ship in one commit; maintainer: a single commit is fine only if the migration runs after all old code stops (i.e. post-deploy).
Maintainer confirms safety_assured skips all checks, including custom ones.
Removing a column default while old Rails processes keep a cached schema can write unexpected NULLs until restart.

included.class: Practitioner uses a linter as a C_{t-1}-vs-S_t gate; reports rule gaps
included.evidence: Team runs squawk in CI to check that the previously deployed version still runs on the new schema; reports that DROP VIEW/FUNCTION/TYPE/TRIGGER and DROP DEFAULT raise no compatibility rule; maintainer agrees to add rules.

included.class: ORM-generated NOT NULL sequence not flagged
included.evidence: Django-generated SET DEFAULT / UPDATE / SET NOT NULL / DROP DEFAULT migration produced no warning; discussion focuses on locking, not on old-version inserts.
User integrating squawk in CI asks for a way to ignore a specific intentional statement (SET NOT NULL).

excluded.reason: Bug in the search importer (hard-coded ids vs domains), not a schema-migration or dual-version failure.
Fresh-install task reads a table before it is created; initialisation-order bug, not dual-version.
Self-hosted upgrade migration failure without reproduction; no evidence of version skew.
CREATE INDEX fails due to pending trigger events inside a data migration; not dual-version.
